interactions.mechanism: Additive anticoagulant effect significantly increases bleeding risk
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR closely; consider PPI gastroprotection

interactions.mechanism: NSAID impairs platelet function and may displace warfarin from albumin binding; high bleeding risk
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination; use acetaminophen for pain

interactions.mechanism: NSAID increases bleeding risk via platelet inhibition and GI erosion
interactions.recommendation: Use with extreme caution; monitor INR and for signs of bleeding

interactions.mechanism: Fluoxetine and its metabolite norfluoxetine inhibit CYP2C9, increasing warfarin levels
interactions.recommendation: Reduce warfarin dose and monitor INR when initiating or discontinuing fluoxetine

interactions.mechanism: Mild CYP2C9 inhibition; sertraline has less CYP inhibition than fluoxetine
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR periodically

interactions.mechanism: Omeprazole may slightly inhibit CYP2C19 metabolism of warfarin R-enantiomer
interactions.recommendation: Generally safe; monitor INR when starting or stopping omeprazole

interactions.mechanism: Simvastatin is metabolized by CYP3A4; minimal effect on warfarin metabolism
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR periodically

interactions.mechanism: Carbamazepine is a potent CYP inducer, significantly reducing warfarin levels
interactions.recommendation: Increase warfarin dose; frequent INR monitoring required

interactions.mechanism: Amiodarone inhibits CYP2C9 and CYP3A4, significantly increasing warfarin levels for weeks
interactions.recommendation: Reduce warfarin dose by 30-50%; monitor INR closely for months

interactions.mechanism: Ibuprofen may competitively inhibit aspirin's irreversible platelet binding, reducing cardioprotection
interactions.recommendation: Take aspirin 30 minutes before ibuprofen; or use alternative analgesic

interactions.mechanism: Combined serotonergic effect causes serotonin syndrome risk
interactions.recommendation: Do not combine two SSRIs

interactions.mechanism: Combined serotonergic effect causes serotonin syndrome risk
interactions.recommendation: Do not combine two SSRIs

interactions.mechanism: Dual RAAS blockade increases risk of hyperkalemia, hypotension, and renal failure
interactions.recommendation: Do not combine ACE inhibitor with ARB

interactions.mechanism: ACE inhibitors reduce aldosterone, causing potassium retention
interactions.recommendation: Monitor potassium levels; avoid potassium supplements unless deficient

interactions.mechanism: Amiodarone inhibits CYP3A4, increasing simvastatin levels and rhabdomyolysis risk
interactions.recommendation: Limit simvastatin to 20mg/day when combined with amiodarone

interactions.mechanism: Cyclosporine dramatically increases simvastatin levels via OATP transport inhibition
interactions.recommendation: Do not combine; use pravastatin or fluvastatin instead

interactions.mechanism: Amiodarone inhibits P-glycoprotein, increasing digoxin levels by 50-100%
interactions.recommendation: Reduce digoxin dose by 50%; monitor levels closely

interactions.mechanism: Verapamil inhibits P-glycoprotein and renal clearance of digoxin
interactions.recommendation: Reduce digoxin dose; monitor levels and heart rate

interactions.mechanism: ARBs may reduce renal function, potentially increasing metformin accumulation risk
interactions.recommendation: Monitor renal function; adjust metformin if eGFR declines

interactions.mechanism: Erythromycin inhibits CYP3A4, increasing carbamazepine levels
interactions.recommendation: Monitor carbamazepine levels; consider azithromycin as alternative antibiotic

interactions.mechanism: Fluoxetine inhibits CYP2D6, increasing metoprolol levels and beta-blockade
interactions.recommendation: Reduce metoprolol dose; monitor heart rate and blood pressure

interactions.mechanism: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, reducing conversion of clopidogrel to active metabolite
interactions.recommendation: Use pantoprazole instead of omeprazole with clopidogrel

interactions.mechanism: Additive CNS depression; increased respiratory depression risk
interactions.recommendation: Start with low doses; monitor respiratory function

interactions.mechanism: Cyclosporine causes potassium retention via mineralocorticoid effects
interactions.recommendation: Monitor potassium; avoid potassium-sparing diuretics
